method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md; atomscan and cleave facts on both supplied archives; extract and trace flagged code; fetch and compare previous releases and official current tarballs. No untrusted package installation or lifecycle execution.

samples.marker: Nuxt DevTools 3.4.4: unchanged Quicktype model; add decode trait
decisive_diff: Both releases declare quicktype-core 22.0.0. Both vendor bundles contain byte-identical gzip and decompressed Markov model data; the changed chunk name is build output.
Decoded model is JSON with trie/depth fields, 1873926 bytes, SHA256 639ba5cb4cf454f81b0c0a6e0735bd57be8103f5fc024cffa6b7a85f4ddb63d4. The 148193-byte gzip header names markov.json.
Current official registry tarball matches the supplied archive byte for byte. Dependency versions and generated client assets changed; cli.mjs remains the same import of @nuxt/devtools-wizard.
trace: The data-schema drawer imports the bundled Quicktype type generator.
encodedMarkovChain is passed to inflateBase64, which calls Base64.atob then the bundled Pako inflate implementation with string output.
load passes the decompressed string to JSON.parse. inferMaps lazily loads the model, and evaluate computes transition probabilities for property names to distinguish map-like keys from object fields.
The decoded bytes are data; this path does not evaluate them as source, launch a process, access credentials, or transmit them.
samples.trait_change: Add notable micro-behaviors/data/compression::javascript-base64-inflate-call, using an invocation query that also handles minifier-generated (0, object.inflateBase64)(data). Symbol facts alone omit that indirect callee.
samples.residual_engine_finding: binary/embedded/base64-gz remains suspicious because embedded_code_detector.rs emits it directly. The same warning reproduces on 3.4.3, contradicting the queue clean-baseline premise under the current engine. This encoding/container observation alone does not establish concealment. YAML cannot change it; no shadow rule or broad exclusion was added.

samples.marker: npm 7.11.1: bundled 7.5.2 birthday art; fix obfuscator claim
decisive_diff: The new package/npm.tgz contains npm 7.5.2, not a modified current birthday command. Its full tarball matches https://registry.npmjs.org/npm/-/npm-7.5.2.tgz byte for byte: SHA256 0c136b7ac737d2e8803c9118b305634d8276cfcc2ec61da7461928169473fd73.
The outer lib/birthday.js is unchanged from 7.11.0 and delegates to @npmcli/npm-birthday. The old obfuscated function is only in the newly shipped nested release.

The outer first-party runtime diff removes the unused always-auth option from adduser and config definitions, consistent with the changelog. Other changes include generated documentation, manifest/dependency updates, and the nested artifact.
Official npm 7.11.1 tarball matches the supplied sample byte for byte.
trace: Nested lib/cli.js dispatches a requested command through npm.commands; lib/npm.js resolves ./<cmd>.js, and cmd-list.js lists birthday as a plumbing command. The birthday module exports a function and has no top-level payload effects.
Numeric Buffer arrays resolve Buffer, from, Date and base64; Base64 strings resolve toString, getFullYear, getUTCDate, getUTCMonth, zlib and inflateSync.

On September 29 UTC it applies Base64 decode -> zlib inflate -> JSON.parse integer array -> Buffer to UTF-8 -> Base64 decode -> zlib inflate -> toString -> console.log. The final 1324 bytes are Unicode party/cake art.

On other dates it returns a Please try again in <milliseconds>ms callback message. Both branches are accounted for. No eval, process launch, file write, credential access or network operation exists in this function.
samples.trait_change: Retain one suspicious signal for real API-name concealment. Move global-buffer-access out of the commercial obfuscator namespace to objectives/anti-static/obfuscation/string/conceal::numeric-buffer-global-key. Replace raw text with a structural query for a numeric Buffer.from array directly used as a global/globalThis key. Remove it from commercial-obfuscation alternatives because it identifies no vendor.
samples.runtime_check_limit: Node, Bun, Deno and standalone JavaScript shells are unavailable. The function and both branches were traced statically, and every compressed layer was decoded independently with Python base64/zlib/json.

focused_controls.contract: Positive fixtures require the new traits. Comments, quoted examples, plain-string Buffer keys, ordinary byte buffers, unrelated receivers, other methods and uncalled inflation references must not acquire those findings. None may imply a commercial obfuscator.
focused_controls.registration: The suspicious positive lives in the taxonomy suite because the general benign validator forbids all suspicious objective findings, regardless of caps. Its relocated content is unchanged from the separately verified positive.
